# Summary

Calculation of key metrics based on the 2023-2024 Aphis fabae phenotyping of the PEAMust collection. 

1) Calculation of the broad-sense heritability ("repeatability") as a function of the number of biological replicates. 
2) Calculation of the correlation between sessions.
3) Decision to keep N biological replicates: compromise between repeatability and number of genotypes/observations. 

# Setup

## Helper functions

Two helper functions are created:\
- `calculate_broad_heritability()` giving the broad sense heritability (H^2^) and the number of genotypes of a given dataset.\
- `create_correlation_plot()` to calculate the correlations between experimental sessions.


```{r}
source("../broad_heritability_function.R")
source("../create_correlation_plot.R")
```

# Broad-sense heritability calculations

## Raw dataset

```{r}
#| echo: true

data250_afabae_00 <- read.csv("../../../../../01.data/2023_screen_specifics_251genotypes/02.aphis_fabae_on_faba_collection/aphis_fabae_fecundity_on_faba_collection_2024-04-02.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, sep = ",") %>%  
  mutate(genotype = as.factor(genotype)) %>% 
  mutate(session = as.factor(session)) 

res <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_00)
```

::: callout-tip
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::

## Missing data

Remove NA values.

```{r}
data250_afabae_01 <- data250_afabae_00 %>% filter(!is.na(larvae_total_number))
data250_afabae_01$genotype <- droplevels(data250_afabae_01$genotype)

res2 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_01)
```

::: callout-tip
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res2$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res2$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res2$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::

```{r}
#| eval: false
create_correlation_plot(data250_afabae_01, 
                         group_cols = c("genotype", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")
```

## Remove observations with no adult alive

We chose to remove all data from plants on which no adult aphid was found. This decision was made to get rid of larvae installation bias and only assess the reproduction ability of the aphid.

When the adult aphid dies, the number of larvae will drop but only because the adult stayed less longer on the plant and not because the plant was not suitable for the reproduction.

```{r}
#| echo: true

data250_afabae_02<- data250_afabae_01 %>% filter(adult_alive != "0") #remove if no adult
data250_afabae_02$genotype <- droplevels(data250_afabae_02$genotype)

res3 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_02)
```

::: callout-note
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res3$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res3$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res3$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::

Heritability strongly increases. 602 measurements are lost. The number of genotype stays the same.

```{r}
#| eval: false
create_correlation_plot(data250_afabae_02, 
                         group_cols = c("genotype", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")
```

```{r normality after adult removal}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 8

# With outliers
p_with <- data250_afabae_02 %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(sample=larvae_total_number)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(y = "Observed quantiles", x = "Theoretical quantiles") +
  ggtitle("With outliers") +
  theme_bw()
p_with
```

A few data outliers (n=3) with high larvae number values seem to be problematic. Let's remove the top 3.

```{r top 3 values}
#| echo: true

# Identify the indices of the top 3 highest values
top_3_indices <- order(data250_afabae_02$larvae_total_number, decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]

# View the top 3 highest values
data250_afabae_02[top_3_indices, ] %>% dplyr::select(genotype, ivip, aphid, larvae_total_number)

# Remove the rows with the top 3 highest values
data250_afabae_03 <- data250_afabae_02[-top_3_indices, ]
```

```{r comparison of qqplots with and without outliers}
#| fig-width: 8

# Without outliers
p_without <- data250_afabae_03 %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(sample=larvae_total_number)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(y = "Observed quantiles", x = "Theoretical quantiles") +
  ggtitle("Without outliers") +
  theme_bw()

p_with + p_without 
```

# Finding the best number of biological replicates criteria

Now the question is: should we filter genotypes for which we have less than X biological repetitions?

Let's extract:   
- The number of genotypes available for X number of biological replicates.\
- The number of observations available for X number of biological replicates.\
- The broad-sense heritability for X number of biological replicates.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

dfb <- data.frame(Column1 = character(), Column2 = character(), Column3 = character())

for (i in 1:12) {
  data <- data250_afabae_03 %>%
    group_by(genotype) %>%           # Group by genotype
    filter(n() >= i) %>%             # Keep only groups with i or more repetitions
    ungroup() 
  data$genotype <- droplevels(data$genotype)
  nlvl<-nlevels(data$genotype)
  
  # Fit the model with a fixed formula
  mod_h2 <- lmer(larvae_total_number ~ (1 | genotype) + (1 | session), data = data)
  
  # Get the variance components
  estimates <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(mod_h2))
  
  # Extract the relevant variance components
  genetic_variance <- estimates$vcov[1]
  residual_variance <- estimates$vcov[3]  # Adjust based on the placement of residual variance
  
  # Get the number of levels for the 'session' random effect
  nbE <- nlevels(data$session)
  
  # Calculate heritability (h2)
  h2 <- genetic_variance / (genetic_variance + (residual_variance / nbE))
  
  nnotation<-nrow(data)
  
  df <- data.frame(Nrep = i, Ngen = nlvl, H2 = h2, Nob = nnotation)
  dfb<-rbind(df, dfb)
}
```
## N observations = f(N biological replicates)

```{r}
ggplot(dfb, aes(x = Nrep, y = Nob)) + 
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1,13,1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,2000)) +
  theme_bw()
```


## N genotypes = f(N biological replicates)
```{r}
ggplot(dfb, aes(x = Nrep, y = Ngen)) + 
  geom_point() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(1,13,1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,250)) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = Ngen), arrow = T) +
  labs(x = "N biological replicates", y = "N genotypes") +
  ggtitle("N genotypes = f(N biological replicates)")
```
## Heritability = f(N biological replicates)

```{r}
ggplot(dfb, aes(x = H2, y = Nrep)) + 
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=seq(1,13,1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,0.4)) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = round(H2,digits = 3))) +
  labs(y = "Number of biological replicates", x = "Broad-sense heritability") +
  ggtitle("Heritability =f(N biol. replicates)")
```

## N observations = f(N biological replicates)

```{r}
ggplot(dfb, aes(x = Nrep, y = Nob)) + 
  geom_point() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,2000)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1,13), breaks = seq(from=1,to=13,by=1)) +
  theme_bw() +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(aes(label = Nob)) +
  labs(y = "Number of observations", x = "Number of biological replicates") +
  ggtitle("N observations = f(N biol. replicates)")
```

:::{.callout-important}
Based on these results, a threshold of >=5 biological replicates seems appropriate. That is keeping all genotypes for which at least 5 biological replicates are available. 
:::

\newpage

# Final filtering: keep genotypes with at least 5 repetitions

```{r broad sense heritability }
#| echo: true
#| eval: true

data250_afabae_04 <- data250_afabae_03 %>%
  group_by(genotype) %>%           # Group by genotype
  filter(n() >= 5) %>%             # Keep only groups with 6 or more repetitions
  ungroup()  
data250_afabae_04$genotype <- droplevels(data250_afabae_04$genotype)

res4 <- calculate_broad_heritability(data = data250_afabae_04)
```

::: callout-important
Conclusions:\
- Heritability is equal to `r round(res4$heritability, digits=3)`.\
- There are `r res4$number_of_genotypes` genotypes in total.\
- There are `r res4$number_of_notation` measurements in total.
:::


```{r}
#| eval: false

create_correlation_plot(data250_afabae_04, 
                         group_cols = c("genotype", "session"), 
                         value_col = "larvae_total_number")
qqnorm(data250_afabae_04$larvae_total_number)
```

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8

p <- data250_afabae_04 %>% 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(sample=larvae_total_number)) +
  stat_qq() +
  stat_qq_line() +
  labs(y = "Observed quantiles", x = "Theoretical quantiles") +
  ggtitle("qqplot of final dataset") +
  theme_bw()
p
```
